The BQm module for the MY component

Source: R/adult-MY-BQm.R
BQm.Rd

Implements a mosquito blood-feeding / egg-laying queue model. Its initialized and parsed state vector tracks blood-feeding (B) and gravid (Q) mosquitoes in uninfected (u), exposed (y), and infectious (z) classes.

State Variables

Bu, By, Bz

uninfected, exposed, and infectious blood-feeding mosquitoes

Qu, Qy, Qz

uninfected, exposed, and infectious gravid mosquitoes

M

total adult mosquito density, derived during parsing

Y

total infected and infectious mosquito density, derived during parsing

Z

total infectious mosquito density, derived during parsing

Dynamical Terms

Lambda or \(\Lambda\)

adult mosquito emergence rate, computed by ramp.xds::Emergence

kappa or \(\kappa\)

net infectiousness, computed by ramp.xds::Transmission

Parameters

f

blood feeding rate — use ramp.xds::setup_f or ramp.xds::setup_blood_feeding_rates

q

human fraction — use ramp.xds::setup_q or ramp.xds::setup_human_fractions

g

mosquito mortality rate — use ramp.xds::setup_g or ramp.xds::setup_mosquito_mortality

sigma_b

emigration rate during blood feeding

sigma_q

emigration rate during egg laying

mu

fraction of emigrating mosquitoes lost

eip or \(\tau\)

extrinsic incubation period

nu or \(\nu\)

egg batch rate — use ramp.xds::setup_nu or ramp.xds::setup_egg_batch_rates

eggsPerBatch or \(\Gamma\)

number of eggs per batch

After basic setup, change_MY_pars.BQm can be used to change parameter values. Bionomic parameters are configured as static baselines by default.

Survival and Dispersal

Blood-feeding and gravid mosquitoes have separate demographic matrices, \(\Omega_b\) and \(\Omega_q\). Each combines mortality \(g\), the corresponding emigration rate (\(\sigma_b\) or \(\sigma_q\)), the emigration-loss fraction \(\mu\), and its dispersal matrix (\(K_b\) or \(K_q\)).

Dynamics

Initialization and output parsing expose six state variables: \(B_u\), \(Q_u\), \(B_y\), \(Q_y\), \(B_z\), and \(Q_z\). The current dMYdt.BQm method instead refers to aggregate \(B\) and \(Q\), which are not returned by get_MY_vars.BQm. Therefore its equations do not currently correspond to the initialized six-state vector.

Infective Biting

The patch-level human biting density, fqM, is based on \(B_u+B_y+B_z\); the infective biting density, fqZ, is based on \(B_z\). F_fqM.BQm and F_fqZ.BQm compute these quantities. ramp.xds::compute_EIR combines fqZ with the biting distribution matrix and resident-bite fraction to compute stratum-level EIR; ramp.xds::F_hbr uses fqM to compute stratum-level HBR.

Egg Laying

Gravid mosquitoes lay eggs at rate \(\nu\); the egg batch rate and number of eggs per batch determine patch-level egg production: $$G=\nu(Q_u+Q_y+Q_z)\Gamma.$$ F_eggs.BQm computes \(G\), which is passed to ramp.xds::EggLaying for distribution among aquatic habitats.
